correctness.rationale: For every group Rota-Baxter operator, B is a homomorphism from the six-element descendant group to S3, so |ker B||Im B|=6. The four possible size pairs are then solved exhaustively using kernel-coset constancy. The (3,2) case gives exactly three parity homomorphisms; the (2,3) case has two possible coset assignments for each transposition kernel and the defining identity eliminates one, while the surviving assignment is the exact-factorization splitting map. For trivial kernel, the inverse crossed homomorphism F yields an endomorphism theta(u)=F(u)u; classifying endomorphisms of S3 shows only theta=1 permits bijective F, giving inversion. The packaged exhaustive checker independently confirms all eight maps, four automorphism orbits, involution pairing, and the cyclic descendant groups.

originality.rationale: The primary paper develops the classification machinery and explicitly motivates classification up to automorphisms and the standard involution, but its S3 discussion concerns extension examples rather than a complete census. The closest same-authors follow-up displays one representative from each of the two non-elementary S3 orbit types and notes that both produce C6 descendant groups, but does not state that only eight operators exist or that those examples exhaust the non-elementary cases. Focused semantic-database and web searches found no eight-operator S3 theorem, four automorphism classes, or two combined equivalence classes.

value.rationale: The primary paper explicitly identifies complete operator classification on a fixed group, modulo automorphisms and the standard involution, as a natural problem. S3 is the smallest nonabelian group and is already used in both primary papers as a test example. The complete census shows that the two previously exhibited non-elementary constructions are not isolated examples but exhaust all non-elementary behavior, and that all six have the same cyclic descendant group despite belonging to two distinct automorphism orbits.
